transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12T16:00:00Z (UTC)
Scheduled duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Collins (Helios VP Platform), Ravi Patel (Helios ML), Sofia Turner (Helios Infra)

Summary: quick scoping call to define acceptance criteria for a 4-week POC focused on latency/throughput SLOs. Primary discussion: first-token latency vs per-token cost and tail metrics (p95/p99), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and practical acceptance gates.

Topics: POC timeline, workload profile, TTFT vs TPOT tradeoffs, sample generation methodology, measurement windows, cold vs warm cache, KV cache priming, canary traffic, pass/fail criteria.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Alex): Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we wanted to run through how we'll size the pilot and what success looks like. I put a short agenda in the invite.
00:22 Speaker 2 (Maya): Thanks Alex, yeah high level we want to know if Redwood can hit our latency targets under 24/7 production like loads and for peak spikes we need predictable degradation not full outages.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): Awesome, we'll do two vectors: steady-state throughput where we measure tail TTFT and TPOT under sustained RPS, and spike tests where we run short 10x bursts to see tail blowups.
00:48 Speaker 1 (Alex): Quick clarifying Q — what does Helios consider "success" for the pilot? Is it purely latency, or also cost per tok and reliability?
01:05 Speaker 2 (Maya): Good question. For us success is threefold: 1) TTFT p95 under 400ms and p99 under 1.2s for conversational flows with ~128 tokens average, 2) stable TPOT p95 under 25ms/token p99 under 80ms/token for sustained runs, and 3) no more than 2x degradation during 10x traffic bursts — meaning we want graceful degradation with fallbacks.
01:33 Speaker 4 (Ravi): To add, we need evidence the system can maintain those numbers with our auth flow and with KV caching enabled. We do have long contexts with KV cash — sorry, KV cash, I mean KV cache — for session personalization.
01:50 Speaker 3 (Priya): Good note. We'll test three cache states: cold (empty KV), warm (primed for common prompts), and hot (fully primed). The TTFT delta between cold and warm is usually significant, so we'll capture and report all three.
02:09 Speaker 1 (Alex): On workload sizing can you confirm current QPS and token distribution?
02:18 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Right now production averages 120 req/sec, median payload ~110 tokens, 95th token size ~300 tokens, and we see diurnal peaks to 400 req/sec for short windows. Our priority flows are chat completions and a reranker path for search.
02:36 Speaker 3 (Priya): Ok that'll guide the benchmark. Our baseline plan: replicate the 7-day traffic histogram you share, run a steady state at the 95th-percentile sustained rate (so around 300 RPS for 10 minutes) and measure TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99. Then run burst tests: 10x your baseline for three minutes to capture tail.
03:00 Speaker 2 (Maya): And the measurement windows — are those 10-minute windows enough to get stable p99s? We want confidence in tails not just single-run flukes.
03:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll run each vector three times, different seed for jitter, and provide aggregated histograms plus per-run time series. p99 is noisy, so we'll report bootstrapped confidence intervals and the 95% CI around p99.
03:27 Speaker 4 (Sofia): How will you replicate auth and payload size? We use JWT on the edge and have an internal rate-limiter.
03:38 Speaker 1 (Alex): For the POC we can run a thin proxy that mimics your auth header and rate-limiter, or you can give us a test token. We prefer to avoid production credentials.
03:50 Speaker 3 (Priya): Also we'll instrument two things: server-side telemetry (traces + spans for first byte and token emit) and client-side synthetic timestamps so we can measure TTFT from the client perspective. That lets us cross-check.
04:07 Speaker 2 (Maya): Good. On the target numbers — why are we separating "first-token" and "per-token"? Can Redwood explain tradeoffs in config or model variants?
04:20 Speaker 3 (Priya): Sure. First-token (TTFT) reflects model startup overhead: request scheduling, kernel warmup, KV cache lookups, and first attention pass. Per-token (TPOT) measures generation throughput (decoder efficiency, kernel choices, quantization). You can optimize TTFT with pinned workers / lower cold starts and you optimize TPOT with batching and quantization. But batching helps TPOT at cost of increasing TTFT for small requests.
04:49 Speaker 4 (Ravi): So if we prioritize low TTFT for interactive agents we might accept higher TPOT. For bulk reranking we prefer higher throughput not first token speed.
04:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): Exactly. We'll run playbooks for two configurations: interactive-optimized (small batch size, reserved warm workers) and throughput-optimized (larger batch, quantized model variants). We'll measure both and show tradeoffs in cost $/1000 tokens.
05:19 Speaker 1 (Alex): Any regulatory or residency constraints that change where the pilot must run?
05:27 Speaker 2 (Maya): We need EU data to stay in EU regions for a subset of traffic. For the POC we can use closest region staging in europe-west to validate latency; production would require VPC/private later on.
05:38 Speaker 3 (Priya): Noted. We'll run one benchmark in an EU region and one in us-east to show region delta.
05:45 Speaker 4 (Sofia): About measurement: do we include retries in the metrics or strip them out?
05:51 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll report raw requests and a deduplicated view where we exclude client-side retries. Both will be surfaced so you can see the impact.
06:02 Speaker 2 (Maya): What's the acceptance gate? If some metrics are in the ballpark but p99 misses slightly, do we fail or pass?
06:11 Speaker 1 (Alex): Proposal: pass if all p95 targets are met and p99 is within 25% of target plus an action plan. Failing hard p99s with no mitigation would be a red. We can also define a cost-performance break-even that you accept.
06:28 Speaker 4 (Ravi): We'll accept that conditionally. Provide suggestions for mitigation (e.g., reserved capacity, smaller model, quantize) in the report.
06:38 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll include an appendix mapping mitigations to expected latency/cost delta. For example, 4-bit quantization typically reduces TPOT by ~20-30% at small quality cost; pinned workers reduce TTFT but increase baseline infra cost.
06:55 Speaker 2 (Maya): On sampling and privacy — we will only share anonymized trace IDs and no PII; we'll provide synthetic prompt templates and a scrubbed traffic trace.
07:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): Perfect. For instrumentation we will send a collection script and a small SDK snippet you can run to produce trace CSVs that match our benchmark harness.
07:16 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Timeline check — can we finish the POC within 4 weeks from data handoff?
07:22 Speaker 1 (Alex): Yes, 4 weeks is feasible: week 0 handoff and setup, week 1 baseline and config tuning, week 2 spike and regression tests, week 3 analysis and final report.
07:34 Speaker 2 (Maya): Sounds good. One more question — what about KV cache priming times? We need guidance on how long to exercise sessions to get to warm state.
07:45 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll capture warm-up curves; typically priming takes about 50-200 requests depending on session churn. We'll report time-to-warm for the top flows and include scripts to reproduce priming.
07:59 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Are there recommended synthetic distributions for token lengths? We have bimodal: short chat (20-60 tokens) and long context replies (250-400).
08:09 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll model a mixed distribution that mirrors your 7-day histogram. For clarity we'll show per-class results (short vs long) and combined.
08:19 Speaker 2 (Maya): Ok last thing — what artifacts will you deliver?
08:23 Speaker 1 (Alex): Deliverables: raw latency logs, aggregated histograms for TTFT/TPOT with p50/p95/p99, bootstrap CI for tails, cost estimates per 1000 tokens for each config, mitigation appendix, and a recorded runbook for the test harness.
08:39 Speaker 3 (Priya): Also we'll attach a short playbook: recommended config to hit p95 targets under both EU and US regions, and suggested Dedicated vs Hosted thresholds.
08:50 Speaker 4 (Ravi): Great. If Redwood can't hit p99 for the long-context path we need fallback logic — trickle responses or lower-context model.
08:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll include fallback suggestions and can prototype a canary flow for that.
09:04 Speaker 1 (Alex): Recap of next steps: Ravi to send traffic and prompts by Monday; Priya to run benchmarks and share results by next week; Alex to send contract/security docs.
09:16 Speaker 2 (Maya): Thanks everyone, that covers it.
09:20 Speaker 1 (Alex): Thanks, we'll follow up in email with schedule and links to the test harness repo.

End of transcript.
